name: Matbench: experimental band gap from composition
description: Predict the experimentally measured band gap (eV) of 4604 inorganic compounds from their composition alone. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error over Matbench's five official cross-validation folds.

sources.locator: Zhuo, Mansouri Tehrani and Brgoch (2018): predicting band gaps of inorganic solids by machine learning from composition; source of the measurements.
Dunn et al. (2020): Matbench v0.1 tasks, nested cross-validation protocol and MAE metric.
matbench_v0.1_validation.json (official folds) and stored per-fold predictions of published submissions (pinned commit).
Per-task Matbench v0.1 leaderboard (mean MAE over the five folds).

requirements.datasets: matbench_expt_gap with the official folds. Fetched by python3 scripts/prepare_chemistry.py from pinned sources and verified by SHA-256 (catalog/chemistry-data-lock.json); not redistributed.

evaluation.benchmark: Matbench: experimental band gap from composition
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) floats. Inputs are compositions {'formula': str, 'composition': {element: amount}}. Called once per official Matbench v0.1 fold (five calls, KFold(5, shuffle, random_state=18012019)), each in a fresh process that receives that fold's training inputs with targets and its held-out inputs without targets; info = {'task', 'input_type', 'target', 'unit', 'fold', 'n_train', 'n_test'}. Runs in a separate process that receives only these arguments (no test values), with at most 4 threads (OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS set to 4), no network, no subprocesses and no read access to the repository or prepared data; numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, RDKit and torch are importable; wall-clock limit 170 s per fold. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out mean absolute error in target units (minimize), the Matbench leaderboard metric

limitations: All targets are public in the Matbench files and every sample is a test sample of one fold; candidates or settings tuned on these folds overfit, so treat scores as development scores.

Leaderboard entries were trained without this task's limits (170 s and at most 4 CPU threads per fold, CPU only), so leaderboard values are reference points rather than targets attainable under the same budget.
Polymorphs with the same composition share one value (deduplicated by composition), and 53% of the entries are metals with zero gap; the source states no licence.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.

state_of_the_art.statement: Best mean MAE on the Matbench v0.1 leaderboard for matbench_expt_gap: 0.2865 eV (Darwin), read on 2026-10-10.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the band gap of inorganic solids from their composition.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Band gaps decide whether a material can serve in photovoltaics, LEDs, photocatalysis or electronics; composition-only models screen candidates before structures are known.

papers.title: Predicting the Band Gaps of Inorganic Solids by Machine Learning
papers.primary_goal: Predict experimental band gaps of inorganic solids from composition with machine learning.
papers.task_relation: The task uses the measurements collected there and scores composition-based predictions.
